builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Evolving Infra: Agent-Adaptive LLM Serving at Scale
summary: The method replaces static prefill-decode disaggregated serving (e.g., NVIDIA Dynamo) with runtime-flexible role switching between prefill and decode nodes, an online planner for the PD split, and an agent-aware distributed KV cache manager that uses agent context signals for eviction and transfer. The cost is substantial systems complexity: a distributed KV management layer, an online planner, and decoupled compute/KV infrastructure that presupposes a multi-node GPU cluster. It can fail when workload composition shifts faster than the planner adapts, when agent context-reuse signals are mispredicted causing premature KV eviction, or when the coordination overhead outweighs gains at small scale.
rationale: The technique targets cluster-scale serving infrastructure (up to 256 GPUs) that the reader does not operate, though its PD-disaggregation and agent-aware KV-reuse ideas are worth tracking as they filter into smaller-scale serving stacks.

claims.statement: The method replaces static prefill-decode disaggregated serving (e.g., NVIDIA Dynamo) with runtime-flexible role switching between prefill and decode nodes, an online planner for the PD split, and an agent-aware distributed KV cache manager that uses agent context signals for eviction and transfer. The cost is substantial systems complexity: a distributed KV management layer, an online planner, and decoupled compute/KV infrastructure that presupposes a multi-node GPU cluster. It can fail when workload composition shifts faster than the planner adapts, when agent context-reuse signals are mispredicted causing premature KV eviction, or when the coordination overhead outweighs gains at small scale.
Reduces mean end-to-end request latency by up to 4.1x and P95 TTFT by up to 14x over NVIDIA Dynamo, evaluated on up to 256 GB300 GPUs with GLM-5.2 and Kimi K2.6.
